questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

In 2015, a company electrified the main railway line between two cities in order to decrease the journey time. The work was noisy, expensive and took a long time. What would be the likely outcome of this project?

options.A: External costs increased and private benefits decreased.
options.B: Private benefits decreased and external cost decreased.
options.C: Private benefits increased and private costs increased.
options.D: Private costs increased and external costs decreased.

questions.questionText: Which measure is specifically designed to reduce divergences between private and social costs?

options.A: equal pay legislation
options.B: minimum wage legislation
options.C: the abolition of tuition fees paid by university students
options.D: the introduction of ‘bus only’ lanes in city centres

questions.questionText: Which is an internal economy of scale?

options.A: efficient local transport networks
options.B: improved access to spare parts as a result of industry growth
options.C: lower risks from supplying a wider range of customers
options.D: the training of skilled labour at a college financed by local firms

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the position of a profit-maximising firm in a perfectly competitive industry. MC AC price, cost AR = MR O output What is the correct analysis of this position? profits in number of firms in the short run industry in the long run

options.A: supernormal decrease
options.B: supernormal increase
options.C: normal remain the same
options.D: subnormal decrease

questions.questionText: When a firm doubles its variable inputs, its fixed inputs are unchanged and output less than doubles. What does this illustrate?

options.A: decreasing average cost
options.B: decreasing marginal cost
options.C: diminishing returns
options.D: diseconomies of scale

questions.questionText: Which practices would be classified as price discrimination? charging lower return flight fares from charging higher rail fares to meet Kuala Lumpur to Hong Kong for the additional costs of train passengers who stay overnight on a companies Saturday in Hong Kong

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: To maximise total revenue, up to which point should a monopolist increase output?

options.A: where marginal revenue equals average revenue
options.B: where marginal revenue is maximised
options.C: where marginal revenue is zero
options.D: where price elasticity of demand is zero

questions.questionText: A firm is operating in perfect competition. What will be the effect on the firm’s revenue if it increases its output by 5%?

options.A: Its revenue will be unchanged.
options.B: Its revenue will increase by 5%
options.C: Its revenue will increase by less than 5%.
options.D: Its revenue will increase by more than 5%.

questions.questionText: A firm successfully engages in a policy of predatory pricing. What will happen to the prices charged by the firm in the short run and in the long run? prices in the prices in the short run long run

options.A: rise rise
options.B: rise fall
options.C: fall rise
options.D: fall fall

questions.questionText: What will act as a barrier to collusion between firms?

options.A: an ability to detect price cuts by rivals
options.B: the abolition of anti-trust measures
options.C: the existence of a small number of firms in the industry
options.D: unstable demand conditions for products

questions.questionText: The diagram represents different combinations of good X and good Y.

options.A: UTVW B UVTW C TUVW D WVUT

questions.questionText: A consumer demands two goods, X and Y. The indifference curve diagram shows the effect of a change in the price of one of these goods on the consumer’s equilibrium. good Y I I O good X Which demand curve can be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: B C D price of price of price of price of good X good X good Y good Y
options.D: D D D O O O O quantity of quantity of quantity of quantity of good X good X good Y good Y demanded demanded demanded demanded

questions.questionText: What could prevent a market failure?

options.A: barriers to entry
options.B: building regulations
options.C: growth of firms
options.D: persuasive advertising

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the Gini coefficient for four countries between 1975 and 2010. Gini coefficient for Brazil, Mexico, India and China 1975–2010 55 Brazil 50 Mexico China India Jan 75 Jan 80 Jan 85 Jan 90 Jan 95 Jan 00 Jan 05 Jan 10 Which country made the greatest move towards a more equal income distribution over the period?

options.A: Brazil
options.B: China
options.C: India
options.D: Mexico

questions.questionText: Extra fishing boats start to operate from a local harbour which depends on fishing for its main income. Which action by the local authority is an example of nudge theory?

options.A: distributing leaflets about the need to safeguard fish stocks
options.B: increasing the licence fees for new boats
options.C: insisting that all fish caught are sold to local people
options.D: restricting the areas in which boats can fish

questions.questionText: What is the main disadvantage of government regulation aimed at restricting the profits earned in a monopolistic industry?

options.A: It acts as a disincentive to innovation.
options.B: It cannot take account of externalities.
options.C: It leads to diseconomies of scale.
options.D: It leads to excessive advertising by firms.

questions.questionText: What is an advantage of a ‘creation of property rights’ solution to externalities resulting from river pollution?

options.A: It allows the possibility of a claim for compensation to those harmed.
options.B: It always makes the polluter pay for pollution caused.
options.C: It results in better monitoring by the government of the damage from pollution.
options.D: It will eliminate pollution completely.

questions.questionText: In the UK in 2015 the average wage was £26500 a year. At the same time, certain footballers were earning more than £150000 a week. Which aspect of the theory of wage determination is most likely to explain this wage differential?

options.A: aggressive wage bargaining by the professional footballers’ trade union
options.B: the inclusion in wages of an element of economic rent
options.C: the monopsony structure of the market for professional footballers
options.D: the theory of net advantages

questions.questionText: What is the most effective policy a government could introduce to reduce frictional unemployment?

options.A: cut welfare spending on benefits
options.B: improve information about job vacancies
options.C: reduce tax rates
options.D: raise interest rates

questions.questionText: Which combination is usually found in the least developed countries?

options.A: a high birth rate and a dominant primary sector
options.B: capital-intensive production and a low rate of saving
options.C: labour-intensive production and a declining population
options.D: net inward migration and a low death rate

questions.questionText: The diagram shows selected US labour statistics from 2001 to 2014. 300 65 net new jobs 200 64 employed as a monthly average percentage of 100 63 (thousands) population aged 0 62 16 and over –100 61 –200 60 –300 59 –400 58 –500 2001 05 10 14 year What can be concluded from the diagram about 2001-2014?

options.A: Employment as a percentage of the population aged 16 and over declined continuously.
options.B: In periods when the number of net new jobs was rising the percentage employed increased.
options.C: The natural rate of unemployment was achieved only in 2008.
options.D: The number of unemployed workers fell in all except four years.

questions.questionText: Under conditions of full employment, the Quantity Theory of Money suggests that (other things being equal) the effect of an increase in the velocity of circulation will be to increase

options.A: output.
options.B: prices.
options.C: the demand for money.
options.D: the quantity of money.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with neither government expenditure nor taxation, the initial income is $2000 million. All savings are carried out by consumers, who save 25% of any income received above $2000 million. Businesses plan to invest $2000 million. What is the value of the multiplier?
Which combination of factors is most likely to result in economic growth?

options.A: an increase in management productivity together with a reduction in the hours worked per employee
options.B: increased educational enrolment together with an increase in business regulation
options.C: the discovery of a new raw material deposit together with significant emigration of labour
options.D: the invention of a technology together with the investment to use it in the economy

questions.questionText: A country’s real national income per head increases. What could explain why this might be accompanied by a fall in households’ standard of living?

options.A: a decrease in state welfare payments
options.B: a decrease in the working age population
options.C: an increase in the trade deficit
options.D: an increase in the consumer price index

questions.questionText: A director becomes redundant as the result of a company merger. His salary was $80 000. He is entitled to an annual private pension of $30 000. In his first year after redundancy he earns $40 000 in consultancy fees and saves $8000 by dismissing his gardener. What is the resulting change in measured national income in the first year?
Which cause of economic growth would involve the least cost for present and future generations of a country’s population?

options.A: increased exploitation of a country’s mineral resources
options.B: investment financed by borrowing from abroad
options.C: investment financed by high rates of domestic savings
options.D: technological innovations in productive processes

questions.questionText: What would encourage industrial expansion in a region of high unemployment?

options.A: a rationing system for building development in that region
options.B: a reduction in tax allowances on investment
options.C: a requirement that only local labour may be employed
options.D: an end to nationally negotiated wage rates

questions.questionText: A government currently has a balanced budget. It is considering the possible variations in tax revenue and government expenditure shown. government options tax revenue expenditure W increase increase X increase reduce Y reduce increase Z reduce reduce Which three options are likely to have the potential to move the budget into surplus?
